issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to "Speichern Sie das Ergebnis in einer Variable namens `score_counter`" (define a variable named score_counter), but the template assembly file does not define any such variable and the solution repository defines a variable named `score_cnt` instead. This name mismatch (and missing variable in the template) will confuse students about the expected symbol name and may cause automated checks or grading scripts that look for `score_counter` to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution and template to define the variable as `score_counter dd 0` in the .data section (and use that name in code), or change the problem statement to require `score_cnt` (and add `score_cnt dd 0` to the template). Preferably add `score_counter dd 0` to template_repository/helloWorld.asm and replace `score_cnt` with `score_counter` in solution_repository/helloWorld.asm.

issues.description: The problem statement requires storing the result in a variable named 'score_counter', but the solution implementation declares 'score_cnt'. This mismatch of identifier names for the same conceptual entity (the score counter variable) creates a mapping confusion: students following the problem requirement will not find the expected variable name in the provided solution and may be uncertain which name to use for grading or verification.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the variable in the solution to match the problem statement: change 'score_cnt dd 0' to 'score_counter dd 0' in solution_repository/helloWorld.asm and update any references to use 'score_counter' so all artifacts consistently refer to the same identifier.
